title: Is FXAlchemist Legit? Full 2026 Review
description: FXAlchemist review: what its track record and subscription claims say, why its start dates conflict, and the missing operator and regulator details.
author: Daniel Carter
excerpt: FXAlchemist sells forex software on strong performance claims, but names no operator or regulator and gives conflicting track-record dates.
content:
FXAlchemist sells automated forex software for MetaTrader 4 and 5, with a subscription model and a published track record. The site presents strong performance numbers, but it names no operator, regulator or licence, and its performance dates do not agree with each other. This review sets out what the site says and what we could not check.

Because the product is software you run on your own broker account, the main question is who stands behind the service and how its figures were produced.

FXAlchemist at a Glance

Here is what the site states and what it leaves out.

CategoryWhat the site says
ProductAutomated forex software for MetaTrader 4 and 5
MarketsFive currency pairs, with broker leverage of 1:200 required
Live trading minimumAbout €650 or $650. Currency not confirmed
SubscriptionSilver €39 a month, Gold €99 per three months, Platinum €349 lifetime
FeesSubscription is the only fee stated. No profit share
Refunds14-day money-back guarantee on a support request
Support7 days a week, 9 AM to 8 PM (UTC+2), via Telegram, WhatsApp or email
WithdrawalsHeld with the user's own broker. Withdrawal process not described
Regulator or licenceNot stated
OperatorNot named. Copyright notice only

Items marked as stated come from the platform's own site. We have not tested the software.

The Performance Claims, Examined

Headline return

The site claims up to 5% monthly performance and cites average drawdowns of 1 to 3%. The figures are linked to a third-party track record and to backtests, but the site does not say whether they are net of spreads, swaps or fees.

Inconsistent dates

The site gives different start dates for its live trading record in different sections. A track record is only as clear as its dates, so this inconsistency matters. Summary statistics on the page show placeholder zeros rather than real values.

Member and purchaser numbers

The site cites over 15,000 members and over 2,100 lifetime purchasers. It gives no source for either figure.

Costs Worth Knowing

The site says the subscription is the only cost, but it also runs a countdown on its lifetime plan, a 50% "special deal" and a coupon behind an email signup. Those are sales tactics, not pricing transparency. Compare the monthly and lifetime options in writing, and do not rely on a countdown to decide.

For this review, the standard minimum is 250 in the reader's local currency: AUD 250 in Australia, GBP 250 in the UK, and EUR 250 in the EU. This site does not say which region it serves, so the figure above is the site's own. Ask the operator which currency and amount apply to you.

Who Is Behind the Brand

The site shows only a copyright notice for FXAlchemist and names no legal entity, company number, address or jurisdiction. Its imprint page is linked but was not available for this review. Press logos link to news items, some of which appear to be press releases, and none is labelled as sponsored.

Before You Register: A Short Checklist

  • Ask for the legal operator's name and check it against your national regulator's register.
  • Read the imprint page and confirm the company behind the copyright notice.
  • Ask for the exact live-trading minimum and the currency that applies to you.
  • Check the refund conditions in writing, and ask which start date the track record uses.

Risks to Keep in Mind

Automated strategies can lose money quickly, and the site's own risk warning says most manual retail accounts lose money. Drawdown figures show losses are expected, and backtests cannot guarantee live results. Leverage of 1:200 magnifies both gains and losses.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does FXAlchemist cost to start?

The site lists a live-trading minimum of about €650 or $650 and sells subscriptions from €39 a month. It does not say which currency applies, so confirm the exact amount in its checkout terms.

Is FXAlchemist regulated?

No regulator, licence or registration number is stated. The risk disclaimer refers to a third-country firm, which is a caveat, not a licence claim.

Does FXAlchemist have a refund policy?

The site offers a 14-day money-back guarantee on a support request. Check the exact conditions in writing before you pay.

Does automation remove the risk of losing money?

No. The site's own warning says a large share of retail accounts lose money when trading manually, and past results do not predict future ones. Its drawdown figures show losses are part of the strategy.

Our Verdict on FXAlchemist

FXAlchemist makes strong performance claims, but it names no operator or regulator, gives inconsistent start dates for its track record, and uses urgency tactics in its pricing. Our rating reflects these gaps. We will revisit it once the company and its figures can be confirmed. Start only with money you can afford to lose.
